subject: SCIENCE
title: Heat and Electricity
objective: Identify safe everyday sources and uses through on-screen sorting only.
introduction: The Sun warms a table, a battery powers a safe toy, and a damaged cord needs an adult. How can Maxine use heat and electricity safely?

vocabulary.definition: Energy that moves from a warmer object to a cooler object.
Energy that can make lights, motors, and other devices work.
The ability to cause change or make something work.

activities.instruction: Watch Milo identify everyday energy uses and unsafe electrical situations.
activities.content: Heat is energy transfer related to temperature differences; electricity involves electric charge. Do not touch hot objects, outlets, damaged cords, or loose batteries.

feedback.retry: Check whether heat or electricity is involved, then look for a safe adult-approved use.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: Heat is energy transfer related to temperature differences; electricity involves electric charge. Do not touch hot objects, outlets, damaged cords, or loose batteries.

items.prompt: Milo compares sunlight, a battery, and a damaged cord. Which statement about heat and electricity is true?

options.text: Touch a hot pan
Insert an object in an outlet
Heat moves from warmer to cooler things, and electricity can power devices.
Heat and electricity are exactly the same.

items.explanation: Heat transfers from warmer to cooler objects, while electricity can power lights and devices. Outlets and hot pans can be dangerous.

items.prompt: Maxine sees sunlight warm a tabletop. Which example shows a safe use of energy?

options.text: Touch a hot pan with bare hands
Sunlight can warm surfaces
Insert a fork into an outlet
Short-circuit a battery

items.explanation: Sunlight warming a surface is an ordinary, safe energy observation. Hot pans, outlets, and short circuits can cause burns or shocks.

items.prompt: Milo sees three safe choices and one dangerous choice. Which action is NOT safe?

options.text: Let sunlight warm a surface
Insert an object into an outlet
Use a battery in a safe device
Ask an adult about a damaged cord

items.explanation: Putting an object into an outlet can cause a dangerous shock. Safe batteries, sunlight, and asking an adult avoid that hazard.

items.prompt: Maxine notices a cord with torn covering. What should a child do?

options.text: Repair it while plugged in
Put it in water
Tell a responsible adult and do not touch it.
Hide it under a blanket

items.explanation: A damaged cord may expose dangerous electricity, so a child should stop, avoid touching it, and tell an adult. Water and hiding it increase risk.

items.prompt: Milo wants to use a damaged cord safely. Which choice is best?

options.text: Short-circuit the battery
Have an adult handle the damaged cord
Insert an object in an outlet
Pull the cord by its wires

items.explanation: An adult can inspect and handle a damaged cord safely. Short circuits, outlets, and pulling wires can cause shock or damage.
